items.question: Which subset of $\mathbb{Z}_{10}$ is a subgroup under addition?

options.why: You kept the multiples of 3 below 10. $9 - 3 = 6$ is fine, but $3 - 6 \equiv 7$ escapes.
You chose the odd residues. They miss the identity 0.
You kept a run from 0. $1 - 2 \equiv 9$ escapes.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Apply the test a − b to each candidate.

explain.text: $\{0, 5\} = \langle 5 \rangle$ passes the one-step test. The others fail it, or miss 0. Its size 2 divides 10, as Lagrange requires.

items.question: List the cosets of $H = \{0, 3, 6\}$ in $\mathbb{Z}_9$. Fill $1 + H$ and $2 + H$, smallest first.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Add 1, then 2, to each of 0, 3, 6.

explain.text: $1 + H = \{1, 4, 7\}$ and $2 + H = \{2, 5, 8\}$. With $H$ they split $\mathbb{Z}_9$ into 3 pieces of 3.

items.question: A group has 20 elements. Select all that apply: which could be the order of a subgroup?

options.why: You kept 3. It does not divide 20.
You kept 8. It does not divide 20.
You kept 6. It does not divide 20.

feedback.correct: Right: only divisors of 20 can occur.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Keep the divisors of 20.

explain.text: By Lagrange a subgroup order divides 20, so 1, 4, 5 and 10 pass and 3, 6, 8 fail.

items.question: A group $G$ has order 12. Must it have a subgroup of order 6?

options.text: No: $A_4$ has order 12 and no subgroup of order 6.
Yes: 6 divides 12, so Lagrange gives one.
options.why: You read Lagrange backwards. It rules sizes out; it never promises them.

options.text: Yes: every group of order 12 is cyclic.
options.why: $A_4$ has order 12 and is not cyclic.

feedback.correct: Right. The converse of Lagrange fails.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Recall the A4 example.

explain.text: Lagrange's converse is false. $A_4$ has subgroups of orders 1, 2, 3, 4 and 12 but none of order 6.

items.question: A permutation of $\{1, \dots, 6\}$ has bottom row $3, 6, 1, 5, 4, 2$. Which is its cycle form?

options.why: You read along the bottom row. Follow $k \to \sigma(k)$: $1 \to 3 \to 1$.
You missed the swap of 4 and 5: $\sigma(4) = 5$.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Follow each entry to its image and back.
Not quite. Take the lcm of the cycle lengths.

byKey.prod: You multiplied 3 × 2 × 4. The 2 and the 4 return together after 4 steps.
byKey.sum: You added the lengths. The order is their lcm.

options.text: $-1$: the 5-cycle is even and the swap is odd.

options.why: You counted cycles of length 2 or more. Use $n - c = 7 - 2 = 5$, odd.
Right sign, wrong reason. A 5-cycle is 4 transpositions, so it is even; the swap makes the whole odd.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Count transpositions: k − 1 for a k-cycle.

explain.text: The 5-cycle is 4 transpositions and the swap is 1, so 5 in all: odd. Equally, $n - c = 7 - 2 = 5$.
